A.explanation: This is the gravitational pull of the box on the Earth, equal in size and opposite in direction to $W$ and acting on the other object.

B.explanation: This is the normal contact force of the Earth pushing up on the box, a contact force not a gravitational force and acting on the same object as $W$.

C.explanation: This acts downward in the same direction as $W$ on the box side, so it cannot be the opposite-directed force on the other object.

D.explanation: This is horizontal along the surface, whereas the gravitational pair with $W$ must act along the vertical line joining box and Earth.

hints: Notice that $W$ is drawn acting downward on the box and is a gravitational force due to the Earth pulling the box.
Recall a Newton third law pair must be the same type of force, opposite in direction, and act on two different objects.
Look for the arrow that acts on the Earth rather than on the box, is gravitational in origin, and points opposite to $W$ along the same line.
walkthrough: Identify what $W$ is: the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the box, acting downward on the box toward the centre of the Earth.
State the Newton third law rule: the pair force must be the same type - gravitational - but with the roles reversed, so exerted by the box on the Earth.
It must therefore act on the other object, the Earth, with equal magnitude and opposite direction, so upward along the line joining them.
The upward arrow on the box is a contact normal force, not gravity, and the downward and horizontal arrows do not show the box pulling upward on the Earth.
Only the upward arrow starting within the Earth satisfies type, object, and direction, and this is option A.
